Hi Priya / Alex —

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. We're trying to convert the high-level timelines into a concrete procurement and onramp schedule so Acme AI's Dedicated cluster can be online for their Q3 release window. A few clarifying asks so procurement and the sales motion can converge: 

1) SKU vs delivery cadence: you provided two SKUs in the last quote (QNT-80A and QNT-80B). We need explicit lead times for full-tranche vs staged shipments (i.e., 40/40 split). Can you confirm expected ship weeks and which weeks are subject to change?

2) Partial shipment policy & acceptance criteria: If Quantium can ship a partial tranche earlier (e.g., 20 GPUs), what's the acceptance / test plan window? Will we get early firmware/drivers that match the final tranche?

3) Deposit / PO milestones: Acme wants a 30-day onramp with a committed delivery window. We need to know the invoicing schedule you expect (deposit %, milestone %, final).

4) Alternative SKUs: if QNT-80A has longer lead time, are there nearby compatible variants we can accept (reduced clock, different memory) and what's the perf delta we should anticipate?

Ben / Marissa / Karthik — looping you in to align the Dedicated sizing and to decide on the cloud backfill ask if Quantium can't meet the earliest tranche.

I'll consolidate answers into a short mutual-action timeline we can share with procurement at Acme.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Hi Naomi / Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick responses inline below, and attached is an updated quote with tranche options (Quantium_quote_v3.pdf).

1) SKU vs delivery cadence: QNT-80A (standard bin) — current lead time 18–22 weeks from PO; QNT-80B (high-memory variant) — 24–28 weeks. We can split shipments; typical partial-shipment cadence we've been able to commit to is a 50/50 split delivered ~4 weeks apart, but that depends on the production window and existing queue. We marked the tentative ship weeks in the attached quote (page 2).

2) Partial shipment policy & acceptance: We do support staged acceptance. For partial tranches we provide:
- Early delivery test image and driver bundle (same major driver; minor firmware updates may arrive with later tranches)
- 10-day provisional acceptance window for smoke testing; final acceptance upon full delivery and integration testing (30 days).

3) Deposit / PO milestones: Standard is 30% deposit on PO, 50% upon first tranche shipment, 20% on final shipment. We can accept a 20%/50%/30% split if Acme requires more time on final payment — that will extend ship scheduling by ~1–2 weeks due to allocation constraints.

4) Alternative SKUs: We have a QNT-80A-lite (reduced double-precision perf, same memory) that can ship ~6 weeks earlier than QNT-80A if we reserve a committed batch. Perf delta ~7–12% on peak throughput for transformer inference; we can provide an eval matrix if you want to run quick perf checks.

Attachment: Quantium_quote_v3.pdf (pdf)

Hope this helps — happy to jump on a 30-min call with procurement to lock the PO cadence.

Best,
Priya Raman

Naomi / team —

If Quantium's staggered shipment pushes the initial availability past Acme's hard window, Stratus can offer a temporary backfill option: a committed pool of preemptible A100-equivalent instances reserved for 6–10 weeks. Key bullets: 
- Capacity: up to 60 GPU-equivalents in a single region (us-west) as a stopgap.
- Pricing: premium to spot but discount to on-demand; I'm attaching the CSV with terms and our SLA carveouts (Cloud_backfill_terms.csv).
- Interop: we can pre-provision networking and images so migration to Dedicated (Quantium gear) is a simple cutover once hardware arrives.
- Limitations: preemptible nature means occasional evictions; we guarantee a migration window and persistent KV cache snapshots to minimize warm-up.

On quoting: if you need an explicit line-item for procurement to accept the temporary cloud backfill as an allowable contingency, we can generate a PO-ready quote that lines up with Quantium's tranche weeks.

Team —

Summarizing next steps and decisions we need to push to close the Acme deal on the Q3 timeline. I distilled Priya / Liam's responses and added our recommended path. Please respond inline or mark thumbs-up on the doc in the Drive link.

Summary of vendor constraints
- Quantium: preferred SKU QNT-80A = 18–22w; QNT-80B = 24–28w. Partial tranches supported (50/50 typical) but contingent on production queue. Deposit schedule defaults to 30/50/20.
- Quantium-lite SKU can shift lead time earlier by ~6 weeks with ~7–12% perf hit.
- Stratus (cloud) can provide up to 60 GPU-equivalents as a 6–10 week backfill; preemptible with migration guarantees.

Recommended risk-mitigated plan (for Acme procurement and legal to review)
1) Issue PO for a 40/40/20 staged delivery with Quantium using the 20/50/30 payment split that reduces schedule risk (we accept slightly larger upfront deposit to secure earlier allocation).
2) Simultaneously lock a Stratus contingency quote for 6 weeks to cover the earliest tranche date + 4 weeks buffer. Add as a line-item contingency in the SOW so procurement accepts the option to activate.
3) Run an expedited eval of QNT-80A-lite in our staging (2–3 days) to validate perf delta; if within acceptable bounds, accept the lite batch for the first tranche to accelerate time-to-live.

Action items (owners / ETA)
- Ben: finalize procurement language for contingency line-item and PO breakdown (ETA: 48 hours).
- Marissa: schedule a 30-min call with Quantium procurement and Acme procurement to lock deposit terms (ETA: tomorrow EOD).
- Karthik: spin up the lite-SKU eval image in staging and run the 3 benchmark prompts from the Acme prompt set (ETA: 72 hours).
- Naomi: prepare a one-page mutual action timeline for Acme and attach Quantium quote + Stratus contingency.

Risks to call out
- If Quantium's production queue slips more than 6 weeks, the Contingency window with Stratus will be insufficient and we'll need to renegotiate tranche sizing or accept higher-cost air freight options.
- Finance to confirm acceptable deposit split — if Acme cannot accept >20% upfront, allocation defers and lead times likely extend.

Please reply with any blockers. If I don't see objections, I'll share the mutual-action timeline with Acme and propose the PO cadence on Friday.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
